chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: What do you think about one who arrives in a town—until when should he be shortening, and when should he complete? He said: When you enter a land and are certain that you will stay there for ten days, then perform the salat in full. But if you do not know how long you will stay there, saying, “Tomorrow I will leave, or the day after tomorrow,” then shorten during the period between your arrival and the passing of one month; then when a month is complete for you, perform the salat in full, even if you wish to leave that very hour.

key_terms.شَهْرٌ: the one-month limit after which the ruling changes
key_terms.فَقَصِّرْ: shorten the salat as the ruling of travel
key_terms.مُقَامَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: an intended stay of ten days that changes the prayer ruling
key_terms.مُقَصِّرًا: performing shortened salat as a traveler
key_terms.يُتِمَّ: to perform the salat in full without shortening

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler stop shortening salat if he does not know how long he will stay in a town?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for a traveler who enters a town without knowing how long he will remain there. If he is certain he will stay ten days, he completes the salat; if he remains undecided day by day, he shortens for up to one month, and after a full month he performs the salat in full.
